title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics; parity fixes and version bumps (py/ts/go)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Multiple SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) had divergent auth and retry behaviors and slightly different streaming ergonomics which caused user confusion and client-side bugs. This PR unifies the auth token refresh flow, consolidates retry/backoff configuration (including idempotency-aware defaults), standardizes streaming APIs (async iterators for Python/TS, channel-friendly patterns for Go), and applies parity fixes across language bindings.  What this PR does: - Add a shared auth adapter that centralizes token refresh/expiry handling; replaces per-sdk hacks. - Introduce a small retry policy DSL (max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, jitter, idempotent_methods) and wire to HTTP transport in all SDKs. - Streaming ergonomics: Python/TS streaming clients now expose async iterators and a read()/aclose() pattern; Go client exposes a simplified Receiver interface with Cancel()/Close(). - Parity fixes: align default timeout behavior, error typing, and header propagation across SDKs. - Version bumps: python 1.12.0, typescript 2.6.0, go 0.4.1. - Docs and examples updated, plus changelog entries.  Checklist: - [x] Core auth adapter implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] Retry DSL implemented and integrated into HTTP layer - [x] Streaming API ergonomics implemented for all three SDKs - [x] End-to-end smoke tests against staging API - [x] Docs, examples, and changelog updated - [x] Release versions bumped and package manifests updated  Notes: Most changes are internal API consolidations; surface ergonomics were intentionally designed to keep backwards compatibility while offering a cleaner modern API. Breaking change risk is low but documented in release notes (users using undocumented internal retry hooks may need small updates). For more context see ENG-4521 and ENG-4518.
